If you want to have a real discussion on some topic, voting seems like nothing more than a psychological trinket for manipulating the discussion. Look at how voting is used to manipulate discussion on Reddit, for example. Do you see voting as having some other function in discussion?
What function does voting play in real discussion?

I see it as a way to see what discussion has taken place (the top) versus what discussion is taking place (new) Esp. if the discussion section 50+ comments on it. I also peruse some of the top submission (and not the comments) on profiles to add my thoughts to a subject I think is important but that I may never get a "voat" on it. I like to get my thoughts out and sometimes it adds to the discussion and sometimes it does not. However, when one does look at the top comments, about half the time, I'm not for them. So it turn, it helps facilitate the discussion even further.
Does a linear time format not best serve the function of seeing what discussion has taken place? We can easily jump to the end to see new comments.

I talked to a friend that said she was doing a 5k run the next day, and I asked if I could tag along. I did expecting that they would have spot-registration, and lo, they did! I ran a 5k. Not bad!

Done with our run, we basked in the glow of achievement and took pictures with our medals. Then I had a thought - we weren't all that tired, so...why not do the course over? The friend agreed and we managed to persuade another friend, and the three of us did almost the entire thing again! 'Almost' because cops shooed us away for part of it because the race was over. So we did anywhere between 8.5-9.2k with a 10 minute rest, with very little preparation on my part!

This is very encouraging, seeing how this was my first run. I did c25k about a year ago, then gave up running for other things. I recently took up cycling, which probably saved my life on race day. I'm planning on doing a 10k next month!

Thanks for reading.
Need a place to brag; I almost did a 10k with little preparation.
